traditions/polish-orthodox/summary: The Orthodox church of Poland, drawing its members mainly from Belarusian, Ukrainian and Lemko minorities. Constantinople granted autocephaly in 1924; Moscow, which did not accept that act, issued its own grant in 1948. Its centre is in Warsaw, with a historic heartland in the Podlasie region around Białystok.
traditions/polish-orthodox/distinctives/: Minority church in a majority-Catholic country
Pilgrimage to the Holy Mountain of Grabarka
Did not recognise the Orthodox Church of Ukraine
traditions/polish-orthodox/profile/autho: Holy Tradition, of which Scripture is the summit, interpreted through the seven ecumenical councils, the Fathers and the liturgy; the conciliar mind of the bishops in communion.
traditions/polish-orthodox/profile/salva: Salvation is theosis: union with God by grace through Christ in the Holy Spirit, received in baptism and lived out in faith, repentance, prayer and the sacramental life of the Church.
traditions/polish-orthodox/profile/sacra: Seven principal Mysteries (baptism by triple immersion, chrismation, Eucharist, confession, ordination, marriage, holy unction), with infant communion; leavened bread in the Eucharist.
traditions/polish-orthodox/profile/escha: Expectation of Christ's return, the resurrection and judgement; prayer for the departed and the communion of saints; no doctrine of purgatory.
traditions/polish-orthodox/profile/gover: Metropolitan of Warsaw and All Poland (Sawa since 1998) with the Holy Synod of bishops.
traditions/polish-orthodox/profile/worsh: Byzantine rite in Church Slavonic, with growing use of Polish; Julian calendar.
traditions/polish-orthodox/profile/canon: Old Testament from the Septuagint, including the books Protestants call deuterocanonical (anagignoskomena), and the 27-book New Testament.
traditions/polish-orthodox/status: Active; a few hundred thousand faithful.
traditions/albanian-orthodox/summary: The Albanian Orthodox church proclaimed autocephaly at the Congress of Berat (1922) and was recognised by Constantinople in 1937. When Enver Hoxha declared Albania an atheist state (1967) all religious practice was banned and clergy imprisoned or killed. From 1992 Archbishop Anastasios (Yannoulatos), a Greek missiologist appointed by Constantinople, rebuilt the church almost from nothing, until his death in 2025.
traditions/albanian-orthodox/distinctive: Ministry in a religiously mixed Muslim–Christian society

traditions/albanian-orthodox/profile/gov: Archbishop of Tirana, Durrës and All Albania with the Holy Synod.
traditions/albanian-orthodox/profile/wor: Byzantine rite in Albanian and Greek; Revised Julian calendar.
traditions/albanian-orthodox/profile/can: Old Testament from the Septuagint, including the books Protestants call deuterocanonical (anagignoskomena), and the 27-book New Testament.
traditions/orthodox-church-in-america/su: Descended from the Russian mission to Alaska begun by Valaam monks in 1794 (St Herman of Alaska), the diocese moved to San Francisco (1872) and New York (1905). Cut off by the Russian Revolution, the 'Metropolia' became self-governing, received autocephaly from Moscow in 1970, and took its present name. Its autocephaly is not recognised by Constantinople and several other churches.
traditions/orthodox-church-in-america/di: Russian Alaskan mission and native Alaskan Orthodoxy
English-language liturgy and an American, multi-ethnic identity
St Vladimir's Seminary (Schmemann, Meyendorff) and St Tikhon's Seminary

Metropolitan of All America and Canada with the Holy Synod; All-American Councils include clergy and lay delegates.

traditions/orthodox-church-in-america/st: Active in the United States, Canada and Mexico.
traditions/orthodox-church-of-ukraine/su: Formed at a unification council in Kyiv's St Sophia Cathedral on 15 December 2018, chiefly from the Ukrainian Orthodox Church–Kyiv Patriarchate (1992) and the Ukrainian Autocephalous Orthodox Church, and granted a Tomos of autocephaly by Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew in January 2019. Constantinople holds that Kyiv had always been its canonical territory and that it alone could heal the earlier schisms; Moscow holds that Ukraine is its canonical territory and broke communion with Constantinople. The Ukrainian Orthodox Church historically linked to Moscow continues alongside it.
traditions/orthodox-church-of-ukraine/di: Recognised by Constantinople, Alexandria, Greece and Cyprus; not by Moscow and most others
Growing use of Ukrainian in the liturgy
Rapid parish transfers after Russia's 2022 invasion
traditions/orthodox-church-of-ukraine/pr: Holy Tradition, of which Scripture is the summit, interpreted through the seven ecumenical councils, the Fathers and the liturgy; the conciliar mind of the bishops in communion. Supporters stress Constantinople's prerogative to grant autocephaly; opponents dispute it.
Salvation is theosis: union with God by grace through Christ in the Holy Spirit, received in baptism and lived out in faith, repentance, prayer and the sacramental life of the Church.
Seven principal Mysteries (baptism by triple immersion, chrismation, Eucharist, confession, ordination, marriage, holy unction), with infant communion; leavened bread in the Eucharist.
Expectation of Christ's return, the resurrection and judgement; prayer for the departed and the communion of saints; no doctrine of purgatory.
Metropolitan of Kyiv and All Ukraine with a Holy Synod; the Tomos reserves certain matters (e.g. holy chrism) to Constantinople.
Byzantine rite in Ukrainian and Church Slavonic; moved to the Revised Julian calendar for fixed feasts in 2023.
Old Testament from the Septuagint, including the books Protestants call deuterocanonical (anagignoskomena), and the 27-book New Testament.
traditions/orthodox-church-of-ukraine/st: Active; its recognition remains one of the most divisive questions in world Orthodoxy.
traditions/old-believers/summary: Russian Orthodox Christians who refused Patriarch Nikon's liturgical reforms and the Great Moscow Council of 1666–67 that anathematised the old rites. Persecuted for centuries — Archpriest Avvakum was burned in 1682 — they divided into 'priestly' groups (popovtsy), which later obtained the Belokrinitsa hierarchy (1846), and 'priestless' groups (bezpopovtsy), which concluded that a valid priesthood had ceased. The Moscow Patriarchate lifted the anathemas on the old rites in 1971.
traditions/old-believers/distinctives/0: Two-finger sign of the cross and pre-Nikonian service books
traditions/old-believers/distinctives/1: Strict preservation of ritual, icons and znamenny chant
traditions/old-believers/distinctives/3: Communities in Siberia, the Baltic, Romania (Lipovans), Alaska, Oregon, Brazil and Bolivia
traditions/old-believers/profile/authori: Tradition as embodied in the pre-1650s Russian books and rites, held to be the faithful Orthodox inheritance; the reforms seen as innovation and apostasy.
traditions/old-believers/profile/salvati: Salvation is theosis: union with God by grace through Christ in the Holy Spirit, received in baptism and lived out in faith, repentance, prayer and the sacramental life of the Church.
traditions/old-believers/profile/sacrame: Priestly Old Believers keep the seven Mysteries with their own clergy; priestless communities retain only baptism and confession led by lay elders, holding that the Eucharistic priesthood has lapsed.
traditions/old-believers/profile/eschato: Strong apocalyptic tradition: many early Old Believers saw the reforms and Peter the Great's state as signs of Antichrist.
traditions/old-believers/profile/governa: Belokrinitsa and other priestly hierarchies (metropolitan in Moscow); priestless communities governed by elected lay elders (nastavniki).
traditions/old-believers/profile/worship: Long services in Church Slavonic with znamenny chant, prostrations and ancient icons; Julian calendar.
traditions/old-believers/profile/canon: Old Testament from the Septuagint, including the books Protestants call deuterocanonical (anagignoskomena), and the 27-book New Testament.
traditions/old-believers/status: Active, with perhaps one to two million adherents worldwide (estimates vary widely).
traditions/russian-orthodox-outside-russ: The church of the Russian emigration after the Civil War, organised in 1920–21 and headquartered successively in Sremski Karlovci, Munich and New York. It refused the 1927 declaration of loyalty to the Soviet state by Metropolitan Sergius, canonised the New Martyrs (1981) and was a voice of strict traditionalism. In 2007 it entered canonical communion with the Moscow Patriarchate as a self-governing church.
Canonisation of Tsar Nicholas II and the New Martyrs (1981)
Reunion with Moscow by the Act of Canonical Communion (2007)

traditions/eritrean-orthodox-tewahedo/su: After Eritrea's independence (1993), the Eritrean dioceses of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church obtained autocephaly through the Coptic Orthodox Patriarchate; the first patriarch, Abune Philipos, was consecrated in 1998. It shares the Ge'ez liturgy, broad biblical canon and Miaphysite (often called Monophysite by opponents) Christology of the Ethiopian church. Patriarch Abune Antonios was removed in 2006 amid government involvement and held under house arrest until his death in 2022, a deposition many Orthodox bodies regarded as uncanonical.
traditions/eritrean-orthodox-tewahedo/di: Ge'ez liturgy and the Tewahedo ('made one') Christology
Monastic centres such as Debre Bizen
Close state oversight of religion in Eritrea
traditions/eritrean-orthodox-tewahedo/pr: Scripture and the tradition of the first three ecumenical councils, the Fathers (especially Cyril of Alexandria) and the Ge'ez liturgical books.
Salvation by the grace of the incarnate Word, received through faith, the sacraments, fasting and the life of the church.
Seven sacraments; the Eucharist (Qurban) in the tabot-centred liturgy; circumcision and Old Testament food laws kept as custom.
Resurrection, judgement and prayer for the dead; strong devotion to Mary and the saints.
Patriarch and Holy Synod; strong state influence since 2006.
Ge'ez and Tigrinya liturgy, drums and sistra, extensive fasting (over 180 days a year for the devout).
Broad Ethiopian-tradition canon including Enoch and Jubilees.
traditions/eritrean-orthodox-tewahedo/st: Active; the church of a large share of Eritrea's Christians. Membership statistics are not reliably available.
